“Make each day your masterpiece“

I'm a sunshine transplant from Minnesota,  I've been crafting beautiful hair for over 20 years. Think of me as your personal hairstylist and friend. I love meeting new people and helping them feel their best.

When I'm not behind the chair, you'll find me soaking up the sun with my 5-year-old Boston Terrier, Melo. (I'd love to see pictures of your furry friends too!) I'm a fitness enthusiast, a baking lover, and a total beach bum.

I'm passionate about my craft and always stay up-to-date on the latest trends. Whether you have curly hair, need color correction, or want a trendy balayage, I've got you covered. I'm also a certified extensions specialist so we can add length and volume together.

Let's create your dream hair together!

Talk soon,
J.

Real Instagram photos (via scripts/ig_photos.py) show warm, sunlit salon-chair back-shots of finished color work: golden blonde balayage, bright platinum-blonde balayage, silky brunette, vivid copper red, and a creative pink/magenta color melt, consistent with the owner's bio (balayage, color correction, curly hair, 'sunshine transplant' from Minnesota, beach-lover personality). qa_note: During local QA (Playwright, headless Chromium 149), the .img-reveal clip-path-based scroll reveal (hero photo, both experience photos, all 5 gallery tiles) was observed to sometimes fail to trigger via IntersectionObserver under synthetic/programmatic scrolling in this specific headless browser build, while ordinary .reveal (opacity/transform) elements always triggered correctly. This reproduces identically on the pristine, unmodified templates/light-v2/index.html exemplar (confirmed side-by-side), so it is inherited, unmodified shared-template behavior, not something introduced by this build, and was not patched here since modifying the shared frozen motion system is out of scope for a single-business derivation. Flagging for a pipeline-level look at IntersectionObserver + clip-path interaction across the whole light-v2/dark-v2 batch.
